Implement NPC-001 for Road Rage Taxi.

Repository:
https://github.com/emehtata/roadragetaxi

Target branch:
release/0.15.0alpha

Goal:
Introduce the first properly architected autonomous NPC car.

NPC-001 is intentionally a SMALL vertical slice:
ONE Resident
→ ONE Driver
→ ONE NPC vehicle
→ ONE preplanned route
→ real OSM roads
→ real traffic rules
→ observable/debuggable driving

Do NOT implement a full multi-vehicle traffic simulation yet.

==================================================
1. FIRST: INSPECT THE EXISTING ARCHITECTURE
==================================================

Before changing code, inspect the existing implementation thoroughly.

In particular inspect:

- Resident/person simulation
- existing Resident model and lifecycle
- TrafficWorld
- road graph / OSM way data
- route planning
- traffic-light implementation
- vehicle/taxi movement and physics
- vehicle sprites and rendering
- camera system and camera-follow capabilities
- pedestrian movement architecture
- collision handling
- map/tile streaming
- existing debug/profiling systems
- existing tests

Reuse existing functionality wherever possible.

Do NOT create duplicate implementations of:
- road graph handling
- route finding
- traffic-light discovery
- map/tile handling
- vehicle rendering
- camera handling

If an existing system is incomplete, extend it rather than creating a parallel system.

==================================================
2. CORE DOMAIN MODEL
==================================================

Introduce a clear separation between:

Resident
Driver
NPCVehicle

The conceptual relationship must be:

Resident
   │
   │ owns/drives
   ▼
Driver
   │
   │ controls
   ▼
NPCVehicle

A moving NPC vehicle MUST always have an active Resident driver.

This invariant is fundamental:

    moving NPC vehicle == active driver Resident

Do not allow an autonomous vehicle to exist as a driverless moving vehicle.

Do not make NPCVehicle responsible for Resident identity or decision-making.

Resident represents the person.

Driver represents the active driving activity/state.

NPCVehicle represents the physical vehicle.

Keep these responsibilities clearly separated.

==================================================
3. NPC VEHICLE
==================================================

Create or extend the existing vehicle architecture with an NPC vehicle representation.

The vehicle should contain physical state such as:

- vehicle_id
- driver/resident reference or ID
- position
- heading
- speed
- target_speed
- acceleration
- steering state
- current road/way
- current lane
- route progress
- vehicle state

Do not duplicate vehicle physics that already exists elsewhere.

The vehicle should be renderable using the existing vehicle rendering system.

Initially there is NO need for:
- vehicle-to-vehicle collision avoidance
- realistic tire simulation
- damage simulation
- complex overtaking
- parking AI
- traffic density simulation

However, design the model so these can be added later.

==================================================
4. DRIVER
==================================================

Create a Driver or DriverState abstraction.

It should contain driving-specific state such as:

- resident_id
- vehicle_id
- route
- current route index
- current way
- current lane
- next maneuver
- target speed
- traffic decision
- driving state

The Driver is responsible for making driving decisions.

The Driver should NOT directly perform rendering.

==================================================
5. ROUTE PLANNING
==================================================

Use the existing TrafficWorld route-planning functionality.

Do not implement a second A* or road graph.

For NPC-001:

- select a deterministic origin
- select a deterministic destination
- calculate the route BEFORE spawning the vehicle
- verify that the route contains multiple road segments
- spawn the NPC only after a valid route exists

The first NPC must therefore never spawn and then randomly search for a route while already driving.

The route should be represented explicitly and the driver should progress through it.

Add clear route-progress handling.

The driver must know:

- current route segment
- next route segment
- next maneuver
- final destination

==================================================
6. LANE SELECTION
==================================================

Introduce a small lane-planning abstraction even if NPC-001 only needs simple lane logic.

The architecture should distinguish:

Route planning
    ↓
Lane planning
    ↓
Traffic rules
    ↓
Vehicle controller

For NPC-001 implement enough lane planning to correctly handle:

- right-hand traffic
- straight movement
- right turns
- left turns

The vehicle must not simply follow the center of an OSM way if that would put it in the wrong lane.

Use existing lane/road metadata where available.

If detailed lane data is unavailable, implement a deterministic fallback based on the road geometry.

Do not invent fake lane data globally.

==================================================
7. FINNISH TRAFFIC RULES
==================================================

Create a dedicated traffic-rule decision layer.

Do NOT embed all traffic rules directly into the vehicle movement code.

The rule layer should produce a driving decision, for example:

PROCEED
SLOW
STOP

and provide:

- target speed
- stop position when applicable
- reason
- steering/lane guidance where needed

At minimum NPC-001 must understand:

- speed limits where available
- red traffic lights
- yellow traffic lights
- green traffic lights
- stopping before a red light
- continuing through a green light
- right-hand traffic
- correct lane for the intended maneuver

The traffic-light implementation MUST NOT allow conflicting traffic movements to receive green simultaneously.

Reuse the existing traffic-light/intersection logic.

Do not create a simplistic rule such as:
"if nearest traffic light is green, drive."

The relevant signal must correspond to the NPC's direction/lane/movement.

Yellow should be treated as a transition state, not simply as green.

==================================================
8. VEHICLE CONTROLLER
==================================================

Create a vehicle controller that converts the driver's decision into physical movement.

Keep this separate from traffic rules.

The controller should handle:

- acceleration
- braking
- target speed
- steering
- heading
- position
- route progression

The vehicle should accelerate/decelerate smoothly.

Avoid instantaneous:

speed = target_speed

Avoid instantaneous:

heading = target_heading

Use the existing movement/physics conventions where possible.

==================================================
9. SMOOTH TURNS
==================================================

This is an important NPC-001 requirement.

NPC cars must NOT perform sharp 90-degree pivot turns.

For an intersection:

straight:

──────────────>

right:

──────────╮
          │
          ↓

left:

          ↑
          │
──────────╯

The actual vehicle trajectory must be a smooth curve.

The vehicle should:

1. approach the intersection in the correct lane
2. slow appropriately
3. enter the intersection
4. follow a smooth turning arc
5. align with the correct lane of the outgoing road
6. continue straight after the turn

Do not use a single-point heading flip.

Prefer an approach such as:
- geometric curve
- sampled turn path
- Bézier curve
- clothoid-like approximation
- or another suitable smooth trajectory

Choose the simplest robust solution compatible with the existing coordinate system.

The outgoing heading must match the destination road direction.

==================================================
10. VEHICLE STATE MACHINE
==================================================

Implement a small explicit state machine.

At minimum:

SPAWNING
CRUISING
APPROACHING_INTERSECTION
WAITING
TURNING
ARRIVING

Allow the architecture to support future states such as:

CRASHED
DISABLED
DRIVER_EXITED
ABANDONED
PARKING
DESPAWNING

Do not implement all future behavior now.

The state machine should make the current behavior easy to inspect.

==================================================
11. RESIDENT / DRIVER LIFECYCLE
==================================================

NPC-001 must establish the lifecycle rules needed for future simulation.

When the NPC car is spawned:

1. create/select a Resident
2. establish that the Resident is the driver
3. create the NPC vehicle
4. associate vehicle ↔ Driver ↔ Resident
5. calculate route
6. start driving

Do not create a moving vehicle first and attach a Resident later.

The association must be explicit and testable.

Prepare the architecture for the future case where:

Resident exits vehicle
        ↓
Vehicle remains where it is
        ↓
Vehicle becomes abandoned/disabled

Do NOT implement crash behavior yet unless the existing architecture makes it trivial.

Most importantly:

A crashed/abandoned vehicle must never automatically receive a new driver as a side effect of respawning.

==================================================
12. ONE DETERMINISTIC NPC
==================================================

Create exactly ONE NPC for the initial implementation.

It should be deterministic in debug/test mode.

Do not create random traffic.

The NPC should:

- have a deterministic Resident
- have a deterministic vehicle
- have deterministic origin
- have deterministic destination
- have deterministic route
- start automatically in debug mode
- drive continuously
- eventually reach the destination

Choose coordinates/roads from the existing loaded OSM map in a robust way.

Do not hard-code arbitrary screen coordinates that only work on one camera position.

Prefer selecting valid road graph nodes/ways from the existing road data.

==================================================
13. CAMERA FOLLOW / OBSERVATION
==================================================

Add a simple debug mechanism for following the NPC.

The goal is that I can actually observe the NPC driving.

If the existing camera system supports target following, reuse it.

Provide a debug control such as:

F6 = toggle NPC debug/follow mode

or another key that does not conflict with existing controls.

When enabled:

- camera follows the NPC
- NPC remains visible
- normal camera smoothing is preserved if possible

When disabled:

- normal camera behavior returns

Do not redesign the camera system.

==================================================
14. DEBUG HUD
==================================================

Add a toggleable NPC debug overlay.

For example:

F7 = toggle NPC debug information

Display:

NPC:
  vehicle id
  resident id

Driving:
  state
  speed
  target speed
  acceleration

Road:
  current way
  current lane
  route index
  next maneuver

Traffic:
  traffic-light state
  traffic decision
  decision reason

Navigation:
  destination
  route length
  route progress

The exact presentation should follow the existing debug/HUD style.

Do not permanently clutter the normal game UI.

==================================================
15. WORLD DEBUG VISUALIZATION
==================================================

When NPC debug mode is enabled, optionally render:

- complete planned route
- current route segment
- current lane target
- steering target
- stopping position
- turning trajectory

Use simple debug graphics.

These visualizations are extremely useful for debugging why the NPC behaves incorrectly.

Do not make them part of the normal game rendering path when debug mode is disabled.

==================================================
16. PERFORMANCE
==================================================

NPC-001 must not reintroduce the performance problems recently fixed.

Be especially careful with:

- per-frame O(N) searches through all roads
- per-frame scanning of all traffic lights
- rebuilding static rendering caches
- repeated route planning
- repeated OSM geometry processing
- unnecessary allocations
- synchronous expensive operations

The route must be planned once and reused.

Do not recalculate A* every frame.

Traffic-light lookup should reuse existing mechanisms.

Do not modify the rendering cache architecture unless absolutely necessary.

Use the existing profiler when useful.

==================================================
17. TESTS
==================================================

Add focused unit/integration tests for the new architecture.

At minimum test:

1. A moving NPC vehicle has a Resident driver.

2. A vehicle cannot enter the active driving state without a driver.

3. Route is calculated before driving starts.

4. Route progression advances correctly.

5. Red light produces STOP.

6. Green light allows PROCEED.

7. Yellow is handled as a distinct decision.

8. Vehicle stops before the intersection/stop line rather than inside it.

9. Straight route maintains correct lane.

10. Right turn produces a smooth trajectory.

11. Left turn produces a smooth trajectory.

12. Vehicle exits a turn aligned with the outgoing road.

13. Driver/vehicle/Resident IDs remain consistent.

14. State-machine transitions are valid.

15. Reaching the destination enters ARRIVING.

Do not write brittle tests based on exact floating-point positions unless necessary.

Prefer behavioral assertions with reasonable tolerances.

==================================================
18. ARCHITECTURAL CONSTRAINTS
==================================================

Keep these layers separate:

Resident
    ↓
Driver
    ↓
Route Planner
    ↓
Lane Planner
    ↓
Traffic Rule Engine
    ↓
Vehicle Controller
    ↓
NPC Vehicle

Rendering is separate from all of these.

The traffic AI must not depend on Pygame drawing operations.

The rendering system must not contain driving decisions.

Avoid giant "NPC update" functions containing everything.

Use small, testable components.

Do not over-engineer a generic framework for dozens of future vehicle types yet.

NPC-001 should be simple, but the boundaries must be correct.

==================================================
19. DO NOT IMPLEMENT YET
==================================================

Explicitly do NOT implement:

- multiple NPC cars
- traffic spawning system
- traffic density management
- vehicle-to-vehicle avoidance
- overtaking
- parking AI
- full accident simulation
- pedestrians reacting to vehicles
- public transport AI
- emergency vehicles
- advanced driver personality
- 200,000 resident simulation
- network/multiplayer traffic

Those will come later.

NPC-001 is about proving the architecture with ONE car.

==================================================
20. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
==================================================

NPC-001 is complete only when:

- the game starts normally
- existing gameplay remains functional
- one NPC Resident is created/selected
- exactly one NPC vehicle is associated with that Resident
- the vehicle has a valid preplanned OSM route
- the vehicle starts driving
- it follows right-hand traffic
- it respects the applicable speed limit
- it stops at red traffic lights
- it proceeds at green
- yellow is handled correctly
- it approaches intersections in the correct lane
- it performs smooth left turns
- it performs smooth right turns
- it aligns with the outgoing lane after turning
- it eventually reaches its destination
- the camera can follow the NPC
- debug information can be enabled
- the route and driving decisions can be visually inspected
- no existing performance optimization is regressed
- existing tests continue to pass

==================================================
21. IMPLEMENTATION PROCESS
==================================================

Work incrementally.

First inspect the repository and identify the existing classes/functions that should be reused.

Then implement the smallest vertical slice:

Resident
→ Driver
→ NPCVehicle
→ existing route planner
→ basic lane planner
→ traffic rule engine
→ vehicle controller
→ state machine
→ rendering
→ camera follow
→ debug HUD

Do not make unrelated refactors.

Do not rewrite existing systems simply to fit a preferred architecture.

If an existing class already provides part of the required functionality, extend it.

After implementation:

1. run the relevant tests
2. run the full test suite
3. check for regressions
4. inspect the actual game behavior
5. report any architectural compromises
6. report any remaining limitations

Most importantly, do not declare NPC-001 complete merely because the car moves.

The purpose of this milestone is to establish a sound architecture that can later support many Resident-driven NPC vehicles without having to rewrite the fundamental driving model.
